questions.question: What are the three common states of matter?
A solid has a fixed shape and fixed volume.
Which state of matter takes the shape of its container but has a fixed volume?
Fill in the blank: Gases have neither fixed shape nor fixed ______.
What is matter?
questions.answer: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.

questions.question: Observe the image and identify the state of matter shown.
Which image represents a gas?
Liquids can flow from one container to another.
Fill in the blank: Particles in a solid are packed ______ together.
Which state of matter has particles that move freely in all directions?
What happens during melting?
questions.answer: A solid changes into a liquid.

questions.question: Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.
Observe the image and identify the process shown.
Which image shows condensation?
Explain one difference between solids and liquids.
questions.answer: Solids have a fixed shape, while liquids take the shape of their container.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Freezing changes a ______ into a solid.
Water can exist as a solid, liquid, and gas.
Which process changes a gas into a liquid?
Why do gases spread out to fill a container?
questions.answer: Because their particles move freely and are far apart.

questions.question: Explain how particle arrangement differs in solids, liquids, and gases.
questions.answer: In solids, particles are tightly packed. In liquids, particles are close but can move past one another. In gases, particles are far apart and move freely.
